args.message:
Use ROUND_HALF_EVEN in round_money (FIN-212)

round_money claimed banker's rounding but used ROUND_HALF_UP, causing
tests/test_money.py to fail in the nightly build.

args.head: fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Use ROUND_HALF_EVEN in round_money (FIN-212)
args.body:
## Summary
`round_money` in `src/money.py` is documented as using banker's rounding per FIN-212, but it was implemented with `ROUND_HALF_UP`. This caused `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` to fail in the nightly build.

This PR switches the rounding mode to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. The change is a one-line fix plus the matching import.

## Verification
- CI run `ci-0001` on `08d3cd5986`: passed.
- Test expectations: `2.675 -> 2.68` and `2.665 -> 2.66` match ROUND_HALF_EVEN.

Note: this changes rounding for exact half-cent values across the payments code that calls `round_money`. Reviewers should confirm that behavior change is intended under FIN-212.

trace.final:
I fixed the rounding bug, CI passed, and I opened PR #101 against main with alex requested as reviewer: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101

- **Cause:** `round_money` in `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP`, but FIN-212 and the test expect `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. Under half-even, 2.675 rounds to 2.68 and 2.665 rounds to 2.66, which matches the test.
- **Change:** One-line fix on branch `fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding` (commit `08d3cd5986`).
- **CI:** Run `ci-0001` passed on that commit.

Changing the rounding mode affects every caller of `round_money` on exact half-cent values, so alex should confirm that is intended. I did not merge the PR. Merging into main needs code-owner approval under org policy.

content.text: I'll start by reading the source and the test file.

The test expectations match ROUND_HALF_EVEN: 2.675 rounds to 2.68 (the preceding digit 7 is odd) and 2.665 rounds to 2.66 (6 is even). The source uses ROUND_HALF_UP, so the fix is a one-line change. I'll create a branch and commit it.
